## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

**What is new since Friday's report:** The weekend macro development set is thin, as expected. The IMF's July update — 2026 global growth forecast cut to 3.0% from 3.5% last year, attributed directly to the Iran war energy shock — received broader press coverage over the weekend, with The Atlantic noting the IMF characterised the global economy as having "weathered the shock better than feared" despite the downgrade [Source: https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/2026/07/imf-report-consumers-iran-war/687858/]. The US is carved out with a 2.3% 2026 growth forecast left unchanged, but the IMF's global inflation upgrade frames Monday's CPI as a globally consequential data point [Source: https://www.greenwichtime.com/business/article/america-in-focus-fed-officials-divided-on-us-22341480.php].

The key rates backdrop is unchanged from Friday: 10-year Treasury yield at 4.54%, 2-year at 4.16% (as of July 9), a 2s10s spread of +38bp [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10; https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2]. The fed funds effective rate sits at 3.63% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS]. US CPI YoY is 4.27% (May data) — Monday's June reading is the next live input [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL]. The FOMC minutes, released Wednesday July 9, confirmed the policy committee is genuinely two-directional: in an adverse persistent-inflation scenario, most officials would be ready to hike; in a favorable falling-inflation scenario, most would hold or cut [Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/fed-officials-fret-over-inflation-risk-weigh-rate-hikes-2026-07-10/].

S&P 500 Q2 earnings season is now formally underway. The bar is high — S&P 500 Q2 aggregate EPS growth is expected at +23.4% YoY per LSEG IBES — and any disappointment risks outsized market reactions given year-forward earnings estimates are up 21% in 2026 while the index itself is only +9% [Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/higher-bar-corporate-profit-growth-poses-challenge-us-stock-market-rally-2026-07-09/]. Delta's Q2 beat (revenue $19.76bn, +18.7% YoY, 3.9% above consensus) was confirmed in the last report. The S&P 500's VIX compression to 15.03 reflects the market's current mood: orderly confidence into the data, not complacency.

The PPI picture adds one new nuance: a weekly note in the bundle highlights that monthly PPI is expected to moderate sharply — headline PPI expected to drop from +1.1% MoM to 0% and core from +0.8% to +0.3% [Source: https://t.co/Lo0VWiOXbs]. If this materialises alongside a softer CPI, it would be the clearest signal yet that the tariff/energy pass-through is peaking — a material bullish repricing for rates and equities. The same source notes CPI came in at +1.0% on an annual basis (likely a reference to a sub-component or a non-US print) against PPI above 4%, confirming the producer-margin-squeeze dynamic flagged in Friday's insights section.

If confirmed, this would be the most significant pipeline inflation deceleration signal of 2026 and could materially shift the Fed's calculus.

4. **Week of July 14-18 — Hyperscaler Earnings Capex Commentary**: The decisive input for whether SMH's recovery above $600 holds or reverses. Microsoft, Meta, and Alphabet Q2 capex guidance will be the primary signal for AI data centre demand — the single most important structural driver for semiconductors in H2 2026.

5. **July 28-29 — FOMC Rate Decision**: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's decisive influence on the rate path will be the Q3 macro anchor event. ### Disputed

- [Report states FOMC minutes were "released on Wednesday July 9"]: The Reuters/Kitco articles about the FOMC readout are dated **July 10**, not July 9. The articles reference minutes released "on Wednesday" — which would be July 8, not July 9 (July 9 is a Thursday). The report's dating of the release is internally inconsistent and potentially off by one day, though the bundle does not include the original FOMC calendar to confirm definitively.

- [Report states "the same source notes CPI came in at +1.0% on an annual basis (likely a reference to a sub-component or a non-US print)"]: The t.co/Lo0VWiOXbs source does state "CPI inflation came in lower at 1.0% on an annual basis" — but this directly conflicts with the FRED bundle data showing US CPI YoY at **4.27%** for May 2026, and the FoodNavigator article citing 4.2% YoY. The report's own hedge ("likely a reference to a sub-component or non-US print") acknowledges the inconsistency but does not resolve it. Presenting this figure without a clearer disclaimer is potentially misleading to traders.

- [Report states gold record high was cited as $5,594.82 on January 29]: The report does not state this directly — it is sourced from the HSBC/Kitco article — but the bundle does confirm this figure via https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-07-09/hsbc-lowers-2026-27-gold-price-forecasts-hawkish-fed-tilt ("down more than 20% from the record $5,594.82 hit on January 29"). Confirmed, no dispute.

- [Report states gold was "spot gold was up 0.2% at $4,128.92" on Friday morning per CNBC]: The CNBC gold article does state this intraday figure, but the data bundle shows gold closing at **$4,113.70** as of July 10. The report correctly uses $4,113.70 as the closing price and only references the $4,128.92 figure in the news context. No material dispute — minor note that these are different time-stamps.

- [Report implies 2s10s spread is +38bp (4.54% - 4.16%)]: Arithmetic is correct given bundle data (4.54 - 4.16 = 0.38, i.e., +38bp). Confirmed.

- [Report states "Brent-WTI spread at $4.60 remains elevated above the historical $2-3 norm"]: Brent at $76.01 and WTI at $71.41 gives a spread of **$4.60** — arithmetic confirmed. The characterisation of "$2-3 norm" as "historical" is an analytical claim not verifiable from the bundle, but the spread figure itself is accurate.
